arxiv-1807-03103.creator: Arezoo Khatibi, Omid Khatibi
arxiv-1807-03103.description: Abstract CPU is undoubtedly the most important resource of the computer system. Recent advances in software and system architecture have increased processing complexity, as computing is now distributed and parallel. CloudSim represents the complexity of an application in terms of its computational requirements.

arxiv-2004-01154.title: PEtab — Interoperable Specification of Parameter Estimation Problems in Systems Biology
arxiv-2004-01154.creator: Leonard Schmiester
arxiv-2004-01154.description:
A 2020 arXiv research paper by Leonard Schmiester. Abstract

Reproducibility and reusability of the results of data-based modeling studies are essential. Yet, there has been – so far – no broadly supported format for the specification of parameter estimation problems in systems biology. Here, we introduce PEtab, a format which facilitates the specification of parameter estimation problems using Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML) models and a set of tab-separated value files describing the observation model and experimental data as well as parameters to be estimated.

arxiv-2206-08878.title: BUDDI-MaNGA II: The Star-Formation Histories of Bulges and Discs of S0s 2022 BUDDI-MaNGA II: The Star-Formation Histories of Bulges and Discs of S0s – References
arxiv-2206-08878.creator: Evelyn J. Johnston, Boris Häußler, Keerthana Jegatheesan, Amelia Fraser-McKelvie, Lodovico Coccato, Ariana Cortesi, Yara Jaffé, Gaspar Galaz, Marcelo Mora & Yasna Ordenes-Briceño
arxiv-2206-08878.description: Abstract Many processes have been proposed to explain the quenching of star formation in spiral galaxies and their transformation into S0s. These processes affect the bulge and disc in different ways, and so by isolating the bulge and disc spectra, we can look for these characteristic signatures.

arxiv-2309-15423.title: Prosumers Participation in Markets: A Scalar-Parameterized Function Bidding Approach
arxiv-2309-15423.creator: Abdullah Alawad, Muhammad Aneeq uz Zaman, Khaled Alshehri, Tamer Başar
arxiv-2309-15423.description: Abstract In uniform-price markets, suppliers compete to supply a resource to consumers, resulting in a single market price determined by their competition. For sufficient flexibility, producers and consumers prefer to commit to a function as their strategies, indicating their preferred quantity at any given market price. Producers and consumers may wish to act as both, i.e., prosumers.

arxiv-2503-05457.title: Dependent Directed Wiring Diagrams for Composing Instantaneous Systems
arxiv-2503-05457.creator: Keri D’Angelo, Sophie Libkind
arxiv-2503-05457.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Keri D’Angelo, Sophie Libkind. Directed wiring diagrams can be used as a composition pattern for composing input/output systems such as Moore machines. In a Moore machine, the input parametrizes an internal state and the internal state defines the output. Because the value of the output is shielded from the input by the internal state, Moore machines can compose by connecting the output of any machine to the input of any other machine.

arxiv-2511-09728.title: Regularity and error estimates in physics-informed neural networks for the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation
arxiv-2511-09728.creator: Mohammad Mahabubur Rahman, Deepanshu Verma
arxiv-2511-09728.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohammad Mahabubur Rahman, Deepanshu Verma. Due to its nonlinearity, bi-harmonic dissipation, and backward heat-like term in the absence of a divergence-free condition, the 2 2 -D/ 3 3 -D Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation poses significant challenges for both mathematical analysis and numerical approximation. These difficulties motivate the development of methods that blend classical analysis with numerical approximation approaches embodied in the framework of the physics-informed neural networks (PINNs).

pmc-10605457.creator: Alexis Germán Murillo Carrasco, Tatiane Katsue Furuya, Miyuki Uno, Tharcisio Citrangulo Tortelli, Roger Chammas
pmc-10605457.description: BackgroundHigh-throughput experiments provide deep insight into the molecular biology of different species, but more tools need to be developed to handle this type of data. pmc-11437073.title: Global burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease attributable to high fasting plasma glucose in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021
pmc-11437073.creator: Ziming Yang, Aolin Li, Yuling Jiang, Xiagela Maidaiti, Yinge Wu, Yinzi Jin
pmc-11437073.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) brings heavy clinical and economic burdens to patients worldwide. High fasting plasma glucose (HFPG) was proven to be an important modifiable risk factor. However, the global burden distribution of HFPG-attributable MASLD has not been fully studied. This study aimed to describe the epidemiological distribution and trends of the burden of HFPG-attributable MASLD worldwide.

pmc-11442903.title: Innate immune sensing of danger signals: novel mechanism of heme complex-mediated lytic cell death
pmc-11442903.creator: Chintan Chhatbar, Michael Schulz, Roman Sankowski
pmc-11442903.description: ROS production. The NLRs represent a large family of immune sensor proteins. Most of its members characterized so far were shown to induce pyroptosis. The most extensively profiled member of the NLR family, NLR pyrin domain-containing (NLRP) 3, is an integral component of “inflammasomes” which mediate inflammatory cell death.

pmc-12429932.title: The Effect of a Four-Month Low-Carbohydrate Diet on Visceral Adipose Tissue in Obese Subjects with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD)
pmc-12429932.creator: Ornella Rotolo, Caterina Bonfiglio, Rosa Reddavide, Anna Maria Cisternino, Rosa Inguaggiato, Gianluigi Giannelli, Federico Salomone
pmc-12429932.description: Background: Previous studies have shown a relationship between Visceral Adipose Tissue (VAT) and Hepatic Fat Content (HFC), and increases in HFC are linked to metabolic abnormalities similar to those associated with elevated VAT. Several short-term and long-term studies have supported these findings.

pmc-12615043.title: An Atypical Presentation of Culture-Negative Cryptococcal Meningitis in an Immunocompetent Host With Prior Stroke: A Case Report
pmc-12615043.creator: Julia Siau Fang Ting, Arvind Yerramilli, Fiona Clarke, Sarah Wong, Marjoree Sehu
pmc-12615043.description: Cryptococcal meningitis commonly presents with acute symptoms such as fever and signs of raised intracranial pressure and usually occurs in immunocompromised hosts. A 55-year-old woman presented with worsening cognitive decline, gait disturbance and recurrent falls. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain revealed a prior stroke and ventriculomegaly. A lumbar puncture (LP) showed normal opening pressure.

pmc-12752504.title: Neural crest induction requires SALL4-mediated BAF recruitment to lineage specific enhancers
pmc-12752504.creator: Martina Demurtas, Samantha M Barnada, Emma van Domselaar, Zoe H Mitchell, Laura Deelen, Marco Trizzino
pmc-12752504.description: Neural crest induction begins early during neural plate formation, requiring precise transcriptional control to activate lineage-specific enhancers. Here, we demonstrate that SALL4, a transcription factor associated with syndromes featuring craniofacial anomalies, plays a crucial role in early cranial neural crest (CNCC) specification.

pmc-13677671.title: Metabolite correlation networks reveal complex phenotypes of adaptation-driving mutations
pmc-13677671.creator: Sharon Samuel, Weronika Jasinska, Ezra Sternlicht, Matvey Nikelshparg, Daniel Kleiner, Shai Pilosof, Shimon Bershtein
pmc-13677671.description: Metabolic adaptation is often driven by mutations in pleiotropic genes that affect metabolism globally. However, identifying which phenotypes produced by such mutations drive selection remains difficult. Here, we consider metabolite correlation networks as a systems-level phenotype whose emergent properties reflect the combined effects of biochemical reactions and regulation.
